description: 🚀 Curated list of open-source, self-hosted projects deployable with Docker and docker-compose. Your go-to resource for amazing self-hostable software.

summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of open-source self-hosted applications that can be deployed with Docker and docker-compose.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" style link list rather than software. It groups several hundred self-hostable projects into about two dozen categories such as Productivity, Development, AI & LLMs, Media, Security, Networking, Monitoring, File Sharing, Finance, and Miscellaneous. Each category is a table with a project name and a one-line description. Entries include well-known projects like Nextcloud, Home Assistant, Jellyfin, Vaultwarden, Immich, and Uptime Kuma, plus various alternatives to commercial SaaS tools. The README does not describe install steps, selection criteria, or maintenance policy for the list itself. It contains no per-project links or setup instructions in the text provided.
use_cases: Finding a self-hosted alternative to a commercial SaaS tool
Choosing a media server or *arr stack component
Picking a password manager or identity provider to host
Finding a monitoring or dashboard tool for a homelab
Discovering self-hosted note-taking, wiki, or project management apps
notable: Organized into about 22 categories with a table of contents
Covers a broad range of self-hosted apps from productivity to home automation and AI
Each entry is a short one-line description of the project
Includes alternatives to popular SaaS products such as Notion, Zapier, and Google Photos
caveats: The README states the project is in early development
The list links to projects but does not provide per-entry links or setup instructions in the text
Some entries are marked as sponsored or promoted by GitAds, which the list places at the top
